questions.question: A client receives intermittent HTTP 429 responses with a retry-after header from a model deployment. What should the client do first?

options.text: Wait for the retry-after period and retry with exponential backoff
options.why: Correct. Backoff respects the limit and spreads retries out.

options.text: Retry immediately in a tight loop
options.why: This increases load and keeps the throttling going.
The authentication method does not change rate limits.
A guardrail does not cause a rate limit.

questions.explanation: A 429 means a rate limit was exceeded.

questions.question: Quota for a model is assigned at which level?

options.why: Prompts do not have quota.

options.text: Per subscription, region, model and deployment type
options.why: Correct. Deployments take slices of this quota.
Users do not hold model quota.
Projects do not hold quota.

questions.explanation: Deployments are carved out of the quota available for their model and type.

questions.scenario: An app has a steady base load that needs predictable latency, with short peaks that are three times higher. Failed requests during peaks are unacceptable.
questions.question: Which design is most cost effective?

options.text: Provisioned capacity sized for the base load, with spillover to a standard deployment
options.why: Correct. Reserved capacity serves the base, and spillover absorbs the peaks.

options.text: Provisioned capacity sized for the peak
options.why: Most of it would sit idle and cost money.

options.text: A single standard deployment with no retry
options.why: Peaks would fail with 429 responses.
Batch cannot serve interactive requests.

questions.explanation: Size reserved capacity for the base and let spillover handle peaks.

questions.question: A project must warn the team at 80 percent of its monthly spend and be visible by team. What should you configure?

options.why: Networking does not track spend.
A pinned version does not track spend.

options.text: An Azure budget with alerts, and tags that identify the team
options.why: Correct. Budgets alert at thresholds and tags attribute cost.
This increases spend potential.

questions.explanation: Budgets, alerts and tags manage cost footprints.

questions.question: Which change reduces input token cost when every request begins with the same long policy text?

options.text: Use prompt caching for the repeated prefix
options.why: Correct. The service can reuse the processed repeated prefix, which lowers cost and latency.
Temperature does not affect the token count.
This increases tokens.
Retries add tokens.

questions.explanation: Caching and shorter prompts reduce cost.
